newsitem.title: USA: New Pentagon chief says U.S. can't police world. [CORRECTED 18:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: New Pentagon chief says U.S. can't police world. [CORRECTED 18:42 GMT]

text.p: William Cohen was sworn in on Friday as secretary of defence, the lone Republican member of President Bill Clinton's Cabinet, and pledged to maintain a strong U.S. military without becoming "the world's policeman."

Vice President Al Gore administered the oath to the former senator from Maine in the Oval Office as Clinton looked on. Seven senators from both parties including the chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, South Carolina Republican Strom Thurmond, provided a strong show of bipartisanship.

"We must ensure that our forces are ready to respond to crises whenever and wherever necessary. And we must buy and develop the weaponry that's necessary to ensure our forces have the technological edge to win quickly and decisively," he said. "We cannot become the world's policeman but neither ... can we ever afford to become a prisoner of world events."

Cohen told the Senate committee at his confirmation hearing on Wednesday (corrects from Tuesday) that the United States intended to have its troops out of Bosnia in 18 months, even if the Europeans decide to keep their peacekeepers there longer.

Clinton chose the Republican moderate for the defence job in an effort to provide a centrist government for his second term. The 56-year-old Cohen is a published poet and spy novelist who retired from the Senate this month after a career focused largely on defence and intelligence issues.
Clinton told the ceremony Cohen had always "reached across the divisions of party to strengthen our defences."
"He has never forgotten ... that at the end of every debate stand our soldiers, sailors, airmen and marines, who look to us for leadership, not political strife," he said.
Cohen told Clinton, "Your decision to reach across party lines for this appointment respects the desires of the American people for an approach to public policy that is free of political rancour."

Clinton's stated desire to work with Republicans has marked the early days of his second four-year term and so far they have responded with similar expressions of goodwill. How far this spirit will extend will depend on budget negotiations that begin next month and how hard the Republicans push investigations into potential Clinton administration scandals.

Cohen, his wife Janet Langhart at his side, said one of his top priorities will be to attract and retain the highest quality men and women to serve in the armed forces and reward them with fair pay, housing, health care and other benefits.

Cohen, who replaced William Perry as defence secretary, said he would begin budget deliberations and briefings on defence spending for the fiscal 1998 budget later in the day. Defence is the largest item in the budget.
